- Dragging a marker and then undoing would restore the marker to
  its original position but leave the selection state wrong.
- Undo now also restores the selection highlight for the marker.
- Redo after undo of a drag now works correctly.
- Added tests for drag -> undo -> redo -> drag again.

r49 | priya | 2026-04-06 10:30 | Add user-generated story submission scaffold
- This is the first step toward user-generated story submission
  for v2.0. The submission pipeline is not yet wired to any UI.
- Added a `StorySubmission` data class with fields: title,
  author, content blocks, cover image, tags, and status.
- Added a `StorySubmissionService` that validates a submission
  and queues it for review. Validation checks for empty title,
  content blocks, and duplicate submission hashes.
- The service writes submissions to a local queue file for now;
  network upload comes later.
- No API endpoint exists yet; the service is only callable from
  code.

r50 | marcus | 2026-04-08 13:21 | Fix text overlay scaling on export
- Text overlays scaled incorrectly when exporting at a resolution
  different from the project resolution.
- The overlay transform is now recalculated based on the export
  resolution, not the preview resolution.
- Fixed a related bug where text would clip at the edge of the
  frame when the export aspect ratio differed from the project
  aspect ratio.
- Added an export test with a 16:9 project exported to 1:1.

The key improvements for Tapestry v2.0 are listed as dynamic content adaptation, user-generated story submission, and improved accessibility in the version control log. Record status: current.

r51 | jun | 2026-04-10 09:02 | Add keyboard shortcut for toggling overlay visibility
- Pressing `Shift+H` now toggles all overlays on/off in the
  preview.
- The shortcut is documented in the keyboard shortcut reference
  dialog.
- Overlay visibility state is per-project and persists across
  saves.

r52 | priya | 2026-04-13 14:47 | Improve accessibility: keyboard navigation for timeline
- This is the first accessibility-focused commit for v2.0.
- Timeline can now be navigated with arrow keys when the timeline
  has focus.
- Left/right moves the playhead by one frame; Shift+Left/Right
  moves by one second.
- Up/down moves the selected scene up/down in the scene list.
- Tab order in the timeline panel is now logical: scene list,
  then timeline ruler, then overlay list.
- Focus indicators are visible by default; can be hidden via a
  preference.
- Known issue: screen reader announcements are not yet added;
  that is tracked separately.

r53 | marcus | 2026-04-15 16:38 | Fix color picker contrast in dark mode
- The color picker hex field had poor contrast in dark mode;
  text was nearly invisible.
- Increased contrast for the hex input and the preview swatch.
- Also fixed the color picker not updating when the overlay color
  was changed via the properties panel.

r54 | jun | 2026-04-18 11:20 | Add export notification banner
- When an export completes, a banner appears in the bottom-right
  corner for 5 seconds.
- Banner shows the export file name and a "Show in folder" button.
- Banner is dismissible early with a close button.
- Multiple export completions queue banners; they appear
  sequentially.
r55 | priya | 2026-04-20 10:15 | Refactor export pipeline for maintainability
- Split monolithic export module into three files: `export/controller.py`,
  `export/encoder.py`, and `export/notifier.py`.
- Controller handles job queueing and progress reporting; encoder wraps
  ffmpeg calls; notifier handles the banner and file reveal logic.
- No functional changes intended; existing export tests pass locally.
- Moved shared constants (aspect ratio presets, codec names) into
  `export/constants.py` to avoid circular imports.
- Note: the `--dry-run` flag for the encoder is still experimental and
  not exposed in the UI.

r56 | marcus | 2026-04-22 09:41 | Fix scene transition flicker on rapid timeline scrubbing
- Reported by user testing group: rapid scrubbing over a transition
  caused a one-frame flash of the previous scene.
- Root cause: the preview renderer was caching the wrong frame index
  when the playhead moved more than 30 frames between updates.
- Added a cache invalidation check on playhead delta; also invalidate
  when the active transition duration changes.
- Regression test added: `test_scrub_no_flicker.py` simulates 200 ms of
  random scrubbing across a 2-second transition.
- Performance impact: negligible (< 1 ms per frame on the reference
  laptop).

r57 | jun | 2026-04-24 15:03 | Add story submission form (first pass)
- New dialog accessible from File > Submit Story… (Ctrl+Shift+S).
- Form collects: story title, author name (optional), story text,
  and a single cover image (PNG/JPG, max 5 MB).
- Validation: title required, story text between 100 and 5000
  characters.
- Submissions are saved locally to `~/Tapestry/Submissions/` as JSON
  with a generated UUID; no network upload yet.
- Placeholder success message shown after save.
- Known issues: no draft autosave; the cover image preview is not
  cropped, so large images stretch the dialog.

r58 | priya | 2026-04-27 11:55 | Improve dynamic content adaptation: text reflow engine
- This is the core work for v2.0's dynamic content adaptation.
- Implemented a layout pass that reflows text overlays when the canvas
  aspect ratio changes.
- Reflow uses a three-pass algorithm: measure text width at current
  font size, adjust line breaks, then scale font size down if the
  block exceeds the overlay bounds.
- Minimum readable font size is 12 pt; below that, the engine adds a
  scroll indicator instead of shrinking further.
- Reflow is triggered on export and on preview resize; it is not yet
  triggered on manual overlay resize (tracked as r61).
- Added unit tests for reflow with long titles, multi-paragraph text,
  and mixed font sizes.
- Performance: reflow of a 10-overlay project takes ~40 ms on the CI
  runner; acceptable for now but may need optimisation for very large
  projects.

r59 | marcus | 2026-04-29 14:22 | Fix crash when opening project with missing media files
- Projects referencing deleted or moved media now open with a warning
  dialog instead of crashing.
- Warning lists each missing file path and offers three actions:
  "Locate…" (manual file picker), "Skip" (continue without the clip),
  and "Cancel" (abort open).
- Missing media is marked with a red icon in the timeline; the clip
  still renders as a black frame with a timestamp overlay.
- Added a "Reconnect all" button in the media panel that batch-locates
  missing files in a chosen directory.
- Edge case: if the project file itself is missing, the app still
  shows the generic "Could not open project" error as before.

r60 | jun | 2026-05-02 10:38 | Add export presets for social platforms
- New presets in the export dialog: Instagram (1:1, 1080×1080),
  YouTube (16:9, 1920×1080), TikTok (9:16, 1080×1920), and LinkedIn
  (4:5, 1080×1350).
- Each preset sets resolution, aspect ratio, and bitrate defaults;
  users can still override any value.
- Preset names are localised (en-SG and zh-SG for now).
- The 1:1 export test from r50 still passes with the Instagram preset
  selected.
- Note: the TikTok preset uses a slightly lower bitrate (4 Mbps
  vs 6 Mbps default) to keep file size reasonable for mobile uploads.
r61 | marcus | 2026-05-04 09:15 | Reflow on manual overlay resize
- Reflow now triggers when a user manually resizes an overlay via the
  canvas handles, closing the gap noted in r58.
- Implementation reuses the same three-pass algorithm; no changes to
  the measurement logic were needed.
- Added a debounce of 150 ms on the resize event to avoid reflowing
  on every mouse-move pixel. This keeps the preview responsive on the
  CI runner's software renderer.
- Manual resize reflow is disabled while the user is dragging the
  corner handle (only fires on mouse release). This prevents the
  overlay from "fighting" the user's drag.
- Unit tests extended: resize a text overlay, verify line breaks
  update, and confirm font size is clamped at 12 pt as before.
- Found and fixed a minor issue where the reflow status message in the
  status bar ("Reflowing…") could remain visible if the overlay was
  deleted mid-reflow. The message now clears on overlay removal.

r62 | priya | 2026-05-05 16:40 | Merge branch 'feature/timeline-undo' into develop
- Merged the undo/redo branch for timeline operations.
- Scope: add, delete, reorder, and move of clips/overlays are now
  undoable. Property changes (e.g. font size, color) are not yet
  covered; that is r64.
- Conflict resolution: picked "theirs" for the reflow-related changes
  in overlay_resize.cpp, since r61 touched the same call sites. The
  merged result was verified with the full unit test suite.
- The merge introduced a regression: undo after a "Reconnect all"
  action in the media panel would restore the old missing-file state,
  but the file list in the media panel was not refreshed. Fixed in
  the same commit by emitting a media-list-changed signal after undo.
- Build is green on all three CI configurations (Linux, macOS,
  Windows). No new warnings.

r63 | jun | 2026-05-06 11:22 | Add keyboard shortcuts for timeline editing
- New shortcuts: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z for undo/redo (macOS uses
  Cmd), Delete to remove selected clip, Ctrl+D to duplicate selection.
- Shortcuts are listed in the Edit menu and in the new "Keyboard
  shortcuts" dialog (Help menu). The dialog is a plain text table for
  now; localisation for zh-SG is pending.
- The duplicate shortcut uses the same logic as the existing
  "Duplicate" button; no new code path.
- Remapped the previous Ctrl+D behaviour (which was "deselect all")
  to Ctrl+Shift+A. This is a breaking change for muscle memory; noted
  in the release notes draft.
- Accessibility check: all shortcuts are reachable via menu items, so
  the app remains fully usable without a keyboard.

r64 | marcus | 2026-05-07 13:05 | Undo/redo for property changes (partial)
- Added undo/redo for property edits: font size, font family, text
  colour, background colour, and overlay opacity.
- Implementation uses a simple command pattern: each property change
  pushes a command onto the undo stack. The stack is capped at 50
  entries to bound memory usage.
- Known limitation: property changes made inside the "Adjust" dialog
  (the one that opens on double-click) are not yet undoable. The
  dialog applies changes directly to the model; wiring it to the
  command stack is tracked as r66.
- Undo of a property change does not trigger reflow, even if the font
  size crosses the 12 pt threshold. This is a deliberate choice to
  keep undo fast, but it means the overlay can display at a size
  below the minimum until the next explicit reflow. Will revisit.
- Added unit tests for the command stack (push, pop, cap, redo).

r65 | priya | 2026-05-08 09:30 | Update export presets for Instagram Reels
- The Instagram preset from r60 now uses 9:16 (1080×1920) as the
  default, matching the current Reels format. The old 1:1 default is
  still available as "Instagram (square)".
- Bitrate for the Reels preset is 5 Mbps (was 6 Mbps for the old
  square preset). This keeps file size under 50 MB for a 60-second
  clip, which is the current upload limit for Reels.
- Updated the preset list in the export dialog; the localisation
  strings for en-SG and zh-SG are in sync.
- The r50 1:1 export test now selects "Instagram (square)" explicitly
  instead of relying on the default.

Production Notes Log 2024
Production Notes Log

Next: Priya to draft a one-page narrative premise by end of week. Marcus to start logging the footage metadata. I'll chase the archive permissions.

---

**Entry #002 — 22 Jan 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Review of Priya's premise draft. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Marcus (remote).

Priya's draft is titled "Tapestry: Threads of a City in Transition." It's structured around three "threads": (1) The Land, (2) The People, (3) The Works. Each thread has a set of moments (video clips, audio clips, stills, text) that the user can weave together. The user's "weaving" is the interaction — they can choose to follow a thread linearly or jump between them.

Marcus asked about the "end state" — what happens when the user finishes? Priya said maybe there's no end, just a "gallery" of their own tapestry that they can save or share. Dr. Tan liked that but worried about scope. We agreed to prototype a single thread first (The People) to test the interaction model before building all three.

Also discussed: the title. "Tapestry" is working well. I noted that we should check if the name is already used by any existing interactive project. Marcus said he'd Google it. (He didn't. Will remind him.)

Version: Premise v0.2 (draft).

---

**Entry #003 — 05 Feb 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Editing decisions on The People thread. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

We watched rough cuts of three interview clips. Decisions:

- Clip A (Mrs. Tan, 1985): Keep as is. The audio quality is poor in places but Priya argued the texture is worth it. We'll add a subtle caption noting the recording condition. Don't "clean" it too much.
- Clip B (Mr. Raju, 1978): Cut the first 30 seconds — it's just him adjusting the microphone. Start at his first memory of the neighbourhood. Fadli to do the edit.
- Clip C (Madam Lim, 1992): This one is longer (about 8 min). We decided to break it into two segments with a "pause point" where the user can choose to continue or explore a related still image. Priya will mark the exact timestamp.

The target release date for Project Tapestry is set to 2025-06-30 in the production notes log. Record status: pending verification.

Fadli asked if we should add subtitles for the dialect portions. Yes — English subtitles, but keep the original audio. We'll note in the credits that translations are approximate.

Also: Marcus emailed that the footage metadata is 60% done. He said the 1980s footage is mostly 16mm, transferred to digital. Some labels are faded; he's cross-referencing with the archive index.

---

**Entry #004 — 19 Feb 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Narrative flow discussion. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Dr. Tan.

Dr. Tan brought a printed copy of the narrative flow diagram (v0.3) and we went through it line by line. Main issue: the "branching" logic was too binary. If the user chooses "A," they never see "B." Dr. Tan said that's fine for some moments, but for others, we should allow "echoes" — brief references to the other path even if not fully explored.

Priya proposed a "thread memory" system: the user's choices leave a visual trail (a coloured thread) that they can see in the background. Even if they don't choose a path, they see it faintly in the corner. This keeps the sense of a larger tapestry without forcing the user to complete everything.

I asked about the technical feasibility. Fadli (who wasn't at this session) has been building the prototype in a web framework; I'll ask him if the "thread memory" is doable without heavy custom code. Dr. Tan said to keep it simple for now — a prototype doesn't need the full visual metaphor, just the branching logic.

Decision: For the prototype, we'll implement a simple "visited/unvisited" marker. The visual thread comes later.

---

**Entry #005 — 03 Mar 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Unplanned — Fadli and I met at the lab to debug the prototype.
I tested the echo logic. When I chose path A, I saw a faint reference to path B in the corner — a single line of text, no audio. It felt right. But there's a bug: if the user goes back and changes a choice, the thread line doesn't update — it keeps the old trail. Fadli said he'll fix it next week.

Note: we still haven't decided on the final title. Dr. Tan said he'd discuss with the faculty board. I'll follow up.

---

**Entry #009 — 05 May 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Workshop with student testers, lab. Attended: Fadli, Priya, Wei Jie, 6 testers (students from the faculty).

We ran a small usability session. The testers were given a short scenario: explore the 1980s segment, make a choice at the pause point, and then continue. Results:

- 4 of 6 testers noticed the thread trail. The other 2 didn't see it until it was pointed out.
- 3 of 6 tried to click on the echo text in the corner — they thought it was a link. It isn't. We should either make it clickable or make it look less like a button.
- The pause point itself was clear to all testers. Good.
- One tester said the dialect subtitles were too fast to read. We'll adjust the timing.

Fadli took detailed notes. Priya suggested making the echo text clickable as a "peek" — it would briefly show a hint of the other path without committing the user. Dr. Tan wasn't there, but I think it's worth exploring.

Also: the testers asked if there would be a way to save progress. We hadn't planned for it, but it came up twice. I'll raise it at the next meeting.

---

**Entry #010 — 21 May 2024 (Tue)**
Session: Production meeting, meeting room 2. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus, Dr. Tan.

Dr. Tan opened with a timeline reminder. He said we need to lock the feature set by the end of June to allow enough time for testing and fixes. He asked for a list of must-have vs. nice-to-have. We drafted it on the board:

Must-have:
- Branching logic with visited/unvisited markers
- Pause point with still image
- Subtitles (English, with timing adjustments)
- Thread memory (basic version)
- Mobile layout fix

Nice-to-have:
- Clickable echo text
- Save progress
- Final title and title screen
- Higher-resolution stills

Marcus said the 1980s metadata will be done by mid-June. He also mentioned that some of the reels are in poor condition — the transfer might have colour issues. We said we'd work with what we have.

The planned release date for Tapestry v2.0 is indicated as 2025-03-15 in the production notes log. Record status: pending verification.

Dr. Tan asked if we could push the release earlier, but I said we'd need to confirm the scope first. No decision made.

---

**Entry #011 — 02 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Unplanned — Fadli and I met at the lab to test the mobile fix.

Fadli had rebuilt the layout for smaller screens. The buttons no longer overlap, and the text is larger. The thread memory is still a bit laggy on older phones, but usable. We tested the pause point on a phone — the still image took a few seconds to load, which might be an issue on slower connections. Fadli said he can compress the image.

We also discussed the clickable echo idea. Fadli said it's doable — just add a hover state and a small animation. He'll prototype it for the next review.

I reminded him about the save progress feature. He said it's a bigger task — would need a backend or local storage. We agreed to keep it as nice-to-have for now.

---

**Entry #012 — 16 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Review of the clickable echo prototype. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

Fadli's prototype works. When you hover over the echo text, it expands to a short sentence — a hint of the other path. Clicking it doesn't commit the user; it just shows the hint and then collapses.
**Entry #013 — 30 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Scope review before the July build sprint. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus (via call).

We went through the must-have list from the last session and confirmed what's locked for v2.0. Priya said the subtitles timing is done — she finished the English pass and the timing adjustments for the slower scenes. Fadli confirmed the mobile layout fix is stable after the patch; the lag on older phones is still there but it's acceptable for now. Thread memory basic version is in and holding up in his local tests.

Marcus joined late from the archive. He said the 1980s metadata is done and he's sent it over — the reels are in worse condition than he first thought, so some of the colour correction is going to be rough. He flagged that Reel 4 has a splice about three minutes in and the audio track drops out for a few seconds there. We noted it and said we'd work around it, maybe with a subtitle note or just let it be — it's part of the source material.

Dr. Tan wasn't at this session but he'd emailed earlier asking again about pulling the release date forward. Priya said she'd rather not — the pause point still image is loading slow on 3G and she wants to test the compressed version first. Fadli agreed. We decided the date stays as planned. No change.

The must-have list is now effectively frozen. The nice-to-have items (clickable echo text, save progress, final title screen) are still in the backlog but not part of the v2.0 scope. Fadli said he'll do the echo text as a side task if he has time, but no promises.

---

**Entry #014 — 14 Jul 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Mid-build check-in. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

Fadli showed the compressed pause-point still. It loads much faster — down from about 5 seconds to under 2 on the test phone. Good enough. He's also done a first pass on the branching logic with visited/unvisited markers. The markers show up as a small dot next to the path options. He said it's working but the logic gets a bit tangled when the user goes back and forth between branches. He's patching it.

Priya reported that the English subtitles are in. She's now checking the timing on the scenes with the 1980s footage — the rough audio in Reel 4 means the subtitles drift by half a second there. She's adjusting manually.

We also talked about the title screen. We'd put it in the nice-to-have column, but Priya said it feels odd to release without it. I said I'd check with Dr. Tan. He's been quiet on the creative side lately — mostly asking about dates.

---

**Entry #015 — 28 Jul 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Review of the branching logic fix. Attended: Wei Jie, Fadli, Priya (short).

Fadli's fix works. The visited/unvisited markers now update correctly even when the user backtracks. He also added a small visual cue — the visited path dims slightly. He said it's not in the original spec but it helps. We kept it.

Priya had to leave early. She left a note about the subtitles — the Reel 4 section is done, but she's noticed the timing on the final scene is slightly off because the still image holds for longer than the audio. She's asked Fadli to check the pause point duration. They'll sort it out.

I still haven't heard back from Dr. Tan about the title screen. I'll follow up this week.

---

**Entry #016 — 11 Aug 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Creative review — narrative flow. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus (via call).

This was a longer session. We watched the full build (or as much as is ready) to check the narrative flow, not just the technical bits.

Priya raised a concern about the middle section — the part where the user first encounters the echo text. She said the hint sentence is too long and it gives away too much of the other path. Fadli said he can shorten it, but the hint is generated from the branch summary, so it might need manual editing. We agreed to write a short hint for each branch manually. Priya will draft them.

documents.content:
r55 | priya | 2026-04-20 10:15 | Refactor export pipeline for maintainability
- Split monolithic export module into three files: `export/controller.py`,
  `export/encoder.py`, and `export/notifier.py`.
- Controller handles job queueing and progress reporting; encoder wraps
  ffmpeg calls; notifier handles the banner and file reveal logic.
- No functional changes intended; existing export tests pass locally.
- Moved shared constants (aspect ratio presets, codec names) into
  `export/constants.py` to avoid circular imports.
- Note: the `--dry-run` flag for the encoder is still experimental and
  not exposed in the UI.

r56 | marcus | 2026-04-22 09:41 | Fix scene transition flicker on rapid timeline scrubbing
- Reported by user testing group: rapid scrubbing over a transition
  caused a one-frame flash of the previous scene.
- Root cause: the preview renderer was caching the wrong frame index
  when the playhead moved more than 30 frames between updates.
- Added a cache invalidation check on playhead delta; also invalidate
  when the active transition duration changes.
- Regression test added: `test_scrub_no_flicker.py` simulates 200 ms of
  random scrubbing across a 2-second transition.
- Performance impact: negligible (< 1 ms per frame on the reference
  laptop).

r57 | jun | 2026-04-24 15:03 | Add story submission form (first pass)
- New dialog accessible from File > Submit Story… (Ctrl+Shift+S).
- Form collects: story title, author name (optional), story text,
  and a single cover image (PNG/JPG, max 5 MB).
- Validation: title required, story text between 100 and 5000
  characters.
- Submissions are saved locally to `~/Tapestry/Submissions/` as JSON
  with a generated UUID; no network upload yet.
- Placeholder success message shown after save.
- Known issues: no draft autosave; the cover image preview is not
  cropped, so large images stretch the dialog.

r58 | priya | 2026-04-27 11:55 | Improve dynamic content adaptation: text reflow engine
- This is the core work for v2.0's dynamic content adaptation.
- Implemented a layout pass that reflows text overlays when the canvas
  aspect ratio changes.
- Reflow uses a three-pass algorithm: measure text width at current
  font size, adjust line breaks, then scale font size down if the
  block exceeds the overlay bounds.
- Minimum readable font size is 12 pt; below that, the engine adds a
  scroll indicator instead of shrinking further.
- Reflow is triggered on export and on preview resize; it is not yet
  triggered on manual overlay resize (tracked as r61).
- Added unit tests for reflow with long titles, multi-paragraph text,
  and mixed font sizes.
- Performance: reflow of a 10-overlay project takes ~40 ms on the CI
  runner; acceptable for now but may need optimisation for very large
  projects.

r59 | marcus | 2026-04-29 14:22 | Fix crash when opening project with missing media files
- Projects referencing deleted or moved media now open with a warning
  dialog instead of crashing.
- Warning lists each missing file path and offers three actions:
  "Locate…" (manual file picker), "Skip" (continue without the clip),
  and "Cancel" (abort open).
- Missing media is marked with a red icon in the timeline; the clip
  still renders as a black frame with a timestamp overlay.
- Added a "Reconnect all" button in the media panel that batch-locates
  missing files in a chosen directory.
- Edge case: if the project file itself is missing, the app still
  shows the generic "Could not open project" error as before.

r60 | jun | 2026-05-02 10:38 | Add export presets for social platforms
- New presets in the export dialog: Instagram (1:1, 1080×1080),
  YouTube (16:9, 1920×1080), TikTok (9:16, 1080×1920), and LinkedIn
  (4:5, 1080×1350).
- Each preset sets resolution, aspect ratio, and bitrate defaults;
  users can still override any value.
- Preset names are localised (en-SG and zh-SG for now).
- The 1:1 export test from r50 still passes with the Instagram preset
  selected.
- Note: the TikTok preset uses a slightly lower bitrate (4 Mbps
  vs 6 Mbps default) to keep file size reasonable for mobile uploads.

documents.content:
r61 | marcus | 2026-05-04 09:15 | Reflow on manual overlay resize
- Reflow now triggers when a user manually resizes an overlay via the
  canvas handles, closing the gap noted in r58.
- Implementation reuses the same three-pass algorithm; no changes to
  the measurement logic were needed.
- Added a debounce of 150 ms on the resize event to avoid reflowing
  on every mouse-move pixel. This keeps the preview responsive on the
  CI runner's software renderer.
- Manual resize reflow is disabled while the user is dragging the
  corner handle (only fires on mouse release). This prevents the
  overlay from "fighting" the user's drag.
- Unit tests extended: resize a text overlay, verify line breaks
  update, and confirm font size is clamped at 12 pt as before.
- Found and fixed a minor issue where the reflow status message in the
  status bar ("Reflowing…") could remain visible if the overlay was
  deleted mid-reflow. The message now clears on overlay removal.

r62 | priya | 2026-05-05 16:40 | Merge branch 'feature/timeline-undo' into develop
- Merged the undo/redo branch for timeline operations.
- Scope: add, delete, reorder, and move of clips/overlays are now
  undoable. Property changes (e.g. font size, color) are not yet
  covered; that is r64.
- Conflict resolution: picked "theirs" for the reflow-related changes
  in overlay_resize.cpp, since r61 touched the same call sites. The

r63 | jun | 2026-05-06 11:22 | Add keyboard shortcuts for timeline editing
- New shortcuts: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z for undo/redo (macOS uses

documents.title: Production Notes Log 2024
documents.content:
Next: Priya to draft a one-page narrative premise by end of week. Marcus to start logging the footage metadata. I'll chase the archive permissions.

---

**Entry #002 — 22 Jan 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Review of Priya's premise draft. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Marcus (remote).

Priya's draft is titled "Tapestry: Threads of a City in Transition." It's structured around three "threads": (1) The Land, (2) The People, (3) The Works. Each thread has a set of moments (video clips, audio clips, stills, text) that the user can weave together. The user's "weaving" is the interaction — they can choose to follow a thread linearly or jump between them.

Marcus asked about the "end state" — what happens when the user finishes? Priya said maybe there's no end, just a "gallery" of their own tapestry that they can save or share. Dr. Tan liked that but worried about scope. We agreed to prototype a single thread first (The People) to test the interaction model before building all three.

Also discussed: the title. "Tapestry" is working well. I noted that we should check if the name is already used by any existing interactive project. Marcus said he'd Google it. (He didn't. Will remind him.)

Version: Premise v0.2 (draft).

---

**Entry #003 — 05 Feb 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Editing decisions on The People thread. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

We watched rough cuts of three interview clips. Decisions:

- Clip A (Mrs. Tan, 1985): Keep as is. The audio quality is poor in places but Priya argued the texture is worth it. We'll add a subtle caption noting the recording condition. Don't "clean" it too much.
- Clip B (Mr. Raju, 1978): Cut the first 30 seconds — it's just him adjusting the microphone. Start at his first memory of the neighbourhood. Fadli to do the edit.
- Clip C (Madam Lim, 1992): This one is longer (about 8 min). We decided to break it into two segments with a "pause point" where the user can choose to continue or explore a related still image. Priya will mark the exact timestamp.

The target release date for Project Tapestry is set to 2025-06-30 in the production notes log. Record status: pending verification.

Fadli asked if we should add subtitles for the dialect portions. Yes — English subtitles, but keep the original audio. We'll note in the credits that translations are approximate.

Also: Marcus emailed that the footage metadata is 60% done. He said the 1980s footage is mostly 16mm, transferred to digital. Some labels are faded; he's cross-referencing with the archive index.

---

**Entry #004 — 19 Feb 2024 (Mon)**
Session: Narrative flow discussion. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Dr. Tan.

Dr. Tan brought a printed copy of the narrative flow diagram (v0.3) and we went through it line by line. Main issue: the "branching" logic was too binary. If the user chooses "A," they never see "B." Dr. Tan said that's fine for some moments, but for others, we should allow "echoes" — brief references to the other path even if not fully explored.

Priya proposed a "thread memory" system: the user's choices leave a visual trail (a coloured thread) that they can see in the background. Even if they don't choose a path, they see it faintly in the corner. This keeps the sense of a larger tapestry without forcing the user to complete everything.

I asked about the technical feasibility. Fadli (who wasn't at this session) has been building the prototype in a web framework; I'll ask him if the "thread memory" is doable without heavy custom code. Dr. Tan said to keep it simple for now — a prototype doesn't need the full visual metaphor, just the branching logic.

Decision: For the prototype, we'll implement a simple "visited/unvisited" marker. The visual thread comes later.

---

**Entry #005 — 03 Mar 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Unplanned — Fadli and I met at the lab to debug the prototype.

documents.title: Production Notes Log 2024
documents.content:
I tested the echo logic. When I chose path A, I saw a faint reference to path B in the corner — a single line of text, no audio. It felt right. But there's a bug: if the user goes back and changes a choice, the thread line doesn't update — it keeps the old trail. Fadli said he'll fix it next week.

Note: we still haven't decided on the final title. Dr. Tan said he'd discuss with the faculty board. I'll follow up.

---

**Entry #009 — 05 May 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Workshop with student testers, lab. Attended: Fadli, Priya, Wei Jie, 6 testers (students from the faculty).

We ran a small usability session. The testers were given a short scenario: explore the 1980s segment, make a choice at the pause point, and then continue. Results:

- 4 of 6 testers noticed the thread trail. The other 2 didn't see it until it was pointed out.
- 3 of 6 tried to click on the echo text in the corner — they thought it was a link. It isn't. We should either make it clickable or make it look less like a button.
- The pause point itself was clear to all testers. Good.
- One tester said the dialect subtitles were too fast to read. We'll adjust the timing.

Fadli took detailed notes. Priya suggested making the echo text clickable as a "peek" — it would briefly show a hint of the other path without committing the user. Dr. Tan wasn't there, but I think it's worth exploring.

Also: the testers asked if there would be a way to save progress. We hadn't planned for it, but it came up twice. I'll raise it at the next meeting.

---

**Entry #010 — 21 May 2024 (Tue)**
Session: Production meeting, meeting room 2. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus, Dr. Tan.

Dr. Tan opened with a timeline reminder. He said we need to lock the feature set by the end of June to allow enough time for testing and fixes. He asked for a list of must-have vs. nice-to-have. We drafted it on the board:

Must-have:
- Branching logic with visited/unvisited markers
- Pause point with still image
- Subtitles (English, with timing adjustments)
- Thread memory (basic version)
- Mobile layout fix

Nice-to-have:
- Clickable echo text
- Save progress
- Final title and title screen
- Higher-resolution stills

Marcus said the 1980s metadata will be done by mid-June. He also mentioned that some of the reels are in poor condition — the transfer might have colour issues. We said we'd work with what we have.

The planned release date for Tapestry v2.0 is indicated as 2025-03-15 in the production notes log. Record status: pending verification.

Dr. Tan asked if we could push the release earlier, but I said we'd need to confirm the scope first. No decision made.

---

**Entry #011 — 02 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Unplanned — Fadli and I met at the lab to test the mobile fix.

Fadli had rebuilt the layout for smaller screens. The buttons no longer overlap, and the text is larger. The thread memory is still a bit laggy on older phones, but usable. We tested the pause point on a phone — the still image took a few seconds to load, which might be an issue on slower connections. Fadli said he can compress the image.

We also discussed the clickable echo idea. Fadli said it's doable — just add a hover state and a small animation. He'll prototype it for the next review.

I reminded him about the save progress feature. He said it's a bigger task — would need a backend or local storage. We agreed to keep it as nice-to-have for now.

---

**Entry #012 — 16 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Review of the clickable echo prototype. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

Fadli's prototype works. When you hover over the echo text, it expands to a short sentence — a hint of the other path. Clicking it doesn't commit the user; it just shows the hint and then collapses.

documents.title: Production Notes Log 2024
documents.content:
**Entry #013 — 30 Jun 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Scope review before the July build sprint. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus (via call).

We went through the must-have list from the last session and confirmed what's locked for v2.0. Priya said the subtitles timing is done — she finished the English pass and the timing adjustments for the slower scenes. Fadli confirmed the mobile layout fix is stable after the patch; the lag on older phones is still there but it's acceptable for now. Thread memory basic version is in and holding up in his local tests.

Marcus joined late from the archive. He said the 1980s metadata is done and he's sent it over — the reels are in worse condition than he first thought, so some of the colour correction is going to be rough. He flagged that Reel 4 has a splice about three minutes in and the audio track drops out for a few seconds there. We noted it and said we'd work around it, maybe with a subtitle note or just let it be — it's part of the source material.

Dr. Tan wasn't at this session but he'd emailed earlier asking again about pulling the release date forward. Priya said she'd rather not — the pause point still image is loading slow on 3G and she wants to test the compressed version first. Fadli agreed. We decided the date stays as planned. No change.

The must-have list is now effectively frozen. The nice-to-have items (clickable echo text, save progress, final title screen) are still in the backlog but not part of the v2.0 scope. Fadli said he'll do the echo text as a side task if he has time, but no promises.

---

**Entry #014 — 14 Jul 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Mid-build check-in. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli.

Fadli showed the compressed pause-point still. It loads much faster — down from about 5 seconds to under 2 on the test phone. Good enough. He's also done a first pass on the branching logic with visited/unvisited markers. The markers show up as a small dot next to the path options. He said it's working but the logic gets a bit tangled when the user goes back and forth between branches. He's patching it.

Priya reported that the English subtitles are in. She's now checking the timing on the scenes with the 1980s footage — the rough audio in Reel 4 means the subtitles drift by half a second there. She's adjusting manually.

We also talked about the title screen. We'd put it in the nice-to-have column, but Priya said it feels odd to release without it. I said I'd check with Dr. Tan. He's been quiet on the creative side lately — mostly asking about dates.

---

**Entry #015 — 28 Jul 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Review of the branching logic fix. Attended: Wei Jie, Fadli, Priya (short).

Fadli's fix works. The visited/unvisited markers now update correctly even when the user backtracks. He also added a small visual cue — the visited path dims slightly. He said it's not in the original spec but it helps. We kept it.

Priya had to leave early. She left a note about the subtitles — the Reel 4 section is done, but she's noticed the timing on the final scene is slightly off because the still image holds for longer than the audio. She's asked Fadli to check the pause point duration. They'll sort it out.

I still haven't heard back from Dr. Tan about the title screen. I'll follow up this week.

---

**Entry #016 — 11 Aug 2024 (Sun)**
Session: Creative review — narrative flow. Attended: Wei Jie, Priya, Fadli, Marcus (via call).

This was a longer session. We watched the full build (or as much as is ready) to check the narrative flow, not just the technical bits.

Priya raised a concern about the middle section — the part where the user first encounters the echo text. She said the hint sentence is too long and it gives away too much of the other path. Fadli said he can shorten it, but the hint is generated from the branch summary, so it might need manual editing. We agreed to write a short hint for each branch manually. Priya will draft them.
